headline: Daily Market Snapshot – October 22 2026
summary: US equity futures dropped sharply in premarket on Oct 22 as Middle East tensions and surging oil prices drove a risk-off tone. S&P 500 prior close was 7,757.17; 10-year Treasury yield at 5.13%; Brent crude near $110; gold near $4,088.

headline: Meta Q3 2026 Revenue Surges 26% to $64.6B, Beats Estimates; EPS Weighed by $9.89B Legal Charge
summary: Meta reported record Q3 2026 revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% year-over-year and ahead of the ~$63.3 billion consensus. GAAP EPS came in at $3.83 versus the $3.56 estimate, though would have been ~$7.40 absent a $9.89 billion settlement charge over teen safety lawsuits. Meta raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.65–$7.75.
key_facts: Operating income fell 37% to $12.99B; operating margin 20% vs 40% prior year
Full-year 2026 adj EPS guidance raised to $7.65–$7.75 vs prior $7.10–$7.25

headline: Meta Announces 2-for-1 Class C Non-Voting Share Distribution; New Shares to Trade from January 2027
summary: Alongside Q3 results, Meta announced it will issue one new Class C non-voting share for each existing Class A and Class B share, effectively doubling share count while concentrating voting power. The Class C shares are expected to begin trading in January 2027; the board has not yet set the record or payment date.
key_facts: 1 Class C non-voting share issued per Class A and Class B share held
New shares expected to trade January 2027
Effectively a 2-for-1 split but non-voting structure preserves Zuckerberg control
Board has not set record or payment date

headline: Tesla Q3 2026: Revenue $28.05B Misses Slightly; Adj EPS $0.48 Beats; AI Spending Weighs on Profit
summary: Tesla reported Q3 2026 revenue of $28.05 billion, fractionally below the $28.13 billion consensus, while adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.44 estimate. GAAP net income fell 43% year-over-year to $787 million as AI and Optimus investment ramped. Deliveries reached 486,532 vehicles, and FSD attach rates in North America exceeded 75% of new vehicles.
key_facts: Automotive gross margin 18.1% (excl. credits), up from 16.3% prior quarter
FSD attach rate >75% of new NA deliveries

headline: IBM Q3 2026 Revenue $17.1B Beats Estimates; Software Up 8%, FY Guidance Maintained
summary: IBM reported Q3 2026 revenue of $17.1 billion, up 5% year-over-year (6% at constant currency), beating the ~$16.87 billion consensus. Adjusted EPS of $2.95 surpassed the $2.88 estimate. Software revenue rose 8%, Infrastructure gained 4%, and Consulting was flat. IBM maintained full-year guidance for 4–5% constant-currency revenue growth.
key_facts: Q3 revenue $17.1B vs ~$16.87B estimate (+5% YoY, +6% CC)
FY guidance: +4-5% CC revenue growth maintained

headline: Netflix Q3 2026: Revenue +12% YoY, EPS $0.87 Beats; Q4 Revenue Guidance $13.4B
summary: Netflix reported Q3 2026 revenue growth of 12% year-over-year, consistent with its own forecast, with diluted EPS of $0.87 beating the $0.82 guidance and ~$0.84 consensus. Operating income rose 37% to $4.5 billion with margin expanding to 34.6%. The company guided Q4 2026 revenue to $13.4 billion and raised full-year 2026 guidance to $51.1 billion.
key_facts: Diluted EPS $0.87 vs $0.82 guidance and ~$0.84 consensus
Q4 operating margin guided 26.0% (incl. ~120 bps headcount charge)

headline: Netflix (NFLX) Among S&P 500's Biggest Losers on Oct 22, Shares Down ~5.3%
summary: Netflix shares fell approximately 5.3% on October 22 as the post-earnings sell-off continued. Netflix has declined after each of its last five earnings reports, and the Oct 20 Q3 results triggered a drop despite an EPS beat, consistent with prior patterns of investors selling on results.
key_facts: Stock down ~41% over the past year prior to earnings
Q3 EPS $0.87 beat consensus but stock continues lower

headline: Valero Energy Q3 2026 EPS $23.90 Beats by $3.00; Revenue $46.1B Tops Estimates
summary: Valero Energy reported Q3 2026 EPS of $23.90, beating the $20.90 analyst estimate by $3.00. Revenue of $46.1 billion exceeded the $43.36 billion consensus estimate, driven by robust refining margins amid high oil prices.

headline: Dow Inc. Q3 2026 EPS $0.71 Beats by $0.10; Revenue $11.3B Tops Consensus
summary: Dow Inc. reported Q3 2026 EPS of $0.71, exceeding the $0.61 consensus estimate by $0.10. Revenue of $11.3 billion came in above the $11.21 billion estimate, reflecting improved demand across its materials science segments.

headline: Honeywell Q3 2026: EPS $2.27 Beats by $0.11; Revenue $4.99B Misses Slightly
summary: Honeywell Technologies (the entity retaining the HON ticker after the June 2026 Honeywell Aerospace spin-off) reported Q3 EPS of $2.27, beating the $2.16 estimate by $0.11. Revenue of $4.99 billion came in fractionally below the $5.01 billion consensus.
key_facts: Honeywell Aerospace spun off as HONA on June 29 2026; HON is now Honeywell Technologies

headline: American Airlines Q3 2026 Revenue Record $16.3B (+19% YoY) But Fuel Surge Drives $269M Net Loss
summary: American Airlines reported a record Q3 2026 total revenue of $16.3 billion, up 19.3% year-over-year and above its own guidance range. However, a 67.5% surge in fuel expense (up $1.9 billion) drove a GAAP net loss of $269 million (-$0.41/share). Unit costs excluding fuel rose 3.0%, the best among US network carriers.
key_facts: Q3 revenue $16.3B (+19.3% YoY), above top of guidance range
CASM-ex +3.0% YoY — best among US network carriers

headline: AT&T Q3 2026: Best Service Revenue Growth in 4+ Years; Raises 2026 EPS Outlook; Stock Slumps 6.4%
summary: AT&T reported its best consolidated service revenue growth in more than four years in Q3 2026, adding over one million Advanced Connectivity customers for a second consecutive quarter across fiber, fixed wireless, and postpaid phone. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS outlook and lowered its long-term capex plan. Despite the positive headline, the stock fell approximately 6.4% on October 22.
key_facts: Best consolidated service revenue growth in 4+ years
Added >1M Advanced Connectivity customers (2nd straight quarter)

headline: Blackstone Q3 2026: $63B Inflows; Quarterly Dividend $1.12/Share, Down from $1.29
summary: Blackstone reported $63 billion in inflows for Q3 2026, with flagship strategies outperforming comparable public indices. The board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.12 per share, down from $1.29 in Q2. Total assets under management are estimated near $1.38 trillion.
key_facts: Flagship strategies beat comparable public indices

headline: Brent Crude Tops $110/Bbl as Houthi Strikes Escalate; WTI Nears $100
summary: Brent crude futures rose to approximately $110.40 per barrel on October 21 after Houthi forces struck a Saudi Aramco administrative building, escalating tensions in the Middle East. WTI crude gained $1.45 to $99.27 per barrel. Oil prices have been elevated by the US-Iran war, attacks on Gulf shipping, and supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts: Houthi strike on Saudi Aramco administrative building
At least 18 vessel attacks over two weeks in Gulf region
US-Iran war has disrupted flows through Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb
G7 agreed to release 100M barrels from emergency reserves

headline: WTI Crude Oil Nears $100/Bbl on Middle East Supply Fears, IEA Warns on Diesel Constraints
summary: West Texas Intermediate crude neared $100 per barrel at approximately $99.27, driven by Middle East supply disruptions and the US-Iran conflict. The IEA warned that diesel constraints from the conflict could persist well into 2027, and global petroleum production is projected to fall from a record 106.3 million bpd in 2025 to 101.1 million bpd in 2026.
key_facts: IEA warns diesel constraints could persist into 2027
Global petroleum production projected at 101.1M bpd in 2026 (down from 106.3M bpd in 2025)

headline: Gold Falls Below $4,100/oz as Oil Rally Raises Inflation Concerns; Higher-for-Longer Rate Fears Weigh
summary: Gold dropped more than 1% to approximately $4,088 per ounce on October 22 as surging oil prices renewed inflation concerns and reinforced expectations for a prolonged high Federal Reserve rate environment. Traders are also awaiting next week's Federal Reserve meeting on October 28.
key_facts: Oil rally stokes higher-for-longer Fed rate fears
Gold reached all-time high of ~$5,608/oz in January 2026

headline: Bitcoin Trades Around $82,000–$84,000 Amid Broader Risk-Off; Corporate Bitcoin Consolidation in Focus
summary: Bitcoin traded in a range of approximately $82,000 to $84,300 on October 22, with a modest +1.6% gain on the day. Total cryptocurrency market cap was approximately $2.77 trillion, down slightly. Markets are weighing corporate bitcoin consolidation trends and the impact of Middle East tensions on risk assets.

headline: Ethereum Trades Around $2,400–$2,480 on October 22
summary: Ethereum traded in the $2,402 to $2,477 range on October 22, gaining approximately 1.2% on the day. The 24-hour trading volume was approximately $14 billion.

headline: US 10-Year Treasury Yield Rises to 5.13%, Near Multi-Month High Ahead of Oct 28 Fed Meeting
summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.13% as of October 21, up 1.18 percentage points year-over-year, driven by persistent inflation concerns amplified by the Middle East oil spike. The 2-year yield stood at 4.79% and the 30-year at 5.42%.

headline: Fed Meeting October 28 in Focus; Fed Funds Target ~4%, Inflation Fears Elevated on Oil Surge
summary: The Federal Reserve's next interest rate decision is scheduled for October 28, 2026. The effective federal funds rate is approximately 3.88%–4.00%. With Brent crude above $110 and the 10-year yield at 5.13%, markets are pricing in a prolonged higher-for-longer rate environment. The Fed faces renewed inflation pressure from the Middle East oil shock.

headline: S&P 500 and Dow Futures Drop ~1% in Premarket Following Asian Sell-Off and Middle East Tensions
summary: US equity futures fell sharply in premarket trading on October 22, with S&P 500 futures down approximately 1% and Nasdaq futures down approximately 1.6%. The decline followed an Asian market sell-off overnight and was driven by oil prices surging above $110/bbl amid escalating Middle East conflict and renewed inflation fears. SPY was down 0.99% at $765.43 premarket and QQQ declined 1.75% to $712.50.
key_facts: Asian markets sold off overnight on oil spike and Middle East tensions

headline: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) Leads S&P 500 Gainers on Oct 22 with +9.5% Surge
summary: Super Micro Computer shares surged approximately 9.5% on October 22, leading S&P 500 gainers, supported by the company's recent commencement of Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 rack shipments in September and continued AI server demand. SMCI stock is up approximately 41% year-to-date.
key_facts: SMCI +9.5% on Oct 22, S&P 500 top gainer
Began shipping Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 racks on Sept 23
Stock up ~41% YTD as of early October

headline: Iran Prolongs US Nuclear Talks Ahead of Midterm Elections; Polymarket Odds Drop to 19% on Tech Sell-Off
summary: Iran extended ongoing nuclear negotiations with the US ahead of the November midterm elections, a development that initially boosted equity futures but was offset by rising oil prices and Middle East hostilities. Separately, Polymarket odds for the midterm outcome fell to approximately 19% as Wall Street faced a tech sell-off driven by $111 Brent crude and Tesla earnings.
key_facts: Iran prolongs US nuclear talks ahead of midterm elections
US-Iran fragile ceasefire and stalled nuclear negotiations ongoing
Polymarket midterm odds dropped to ~19% amid tech sell-off
Oil at $111 Brent reinforces geopolitical risk premium

headline: Barclays: Tesla-SpaceX Merger Could Be Announced Before December; Tesla Annual Meeting Dec 3
summary: Barclays analyst Dan Levy said a Tesla-SpaceX all-stock acquisition announcement could come before December, potentially ahead of Tesla's annual shareholder meeting on December 3. Barclays estimates Musk would retain ~37% economic ownership and ~56% voting control in a combined entity. No deal has been confirmed; Tesla's proxy shows an Ehrenpreis director now serving on SpaceX's board as a governance signal.
key_facts: Barclays says deal could be announced before December 2026
Musk estimated to retain ~37% economic ownership and ~56% voting control post-merger
No merger confirmed; analyst speculation only
Tesla proxy reveals Ira Ehrenpreis joined SpaceX board in February 2026

headline: US Dollar Index Slips to ~101.60 as UK CPI Hits 3.5% and Jobless Claims Loom
summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY) eased to approximately 101.60 on October 22, weighed down by a UK CPI print of 3.5% that sparked sterling strength and by anticipation of upcoming US weekly jobless claims data. EUR/USD was near 1.1234 and USD/JPY fell to a one-week low around 157.22.

headline: USD/JPY Hits One-Week Low Near 157.22 in Asian Session on Dollar Weakness
summary: The US dollar fell to a one-week low against the Japanese yen, touching approximately 157.22 during Asian trading on October 22. The decline reflects broader dollar weakness driven by lower Treasury yields and expectations of potential Bank of Japan policy moves, though the yen remains at historically weak levels.
key_facts: USD/JPY ~157.22, one-week low in Asian session
Bears eyeing trading range support near 157.50

headline: Asian Stocks Slide as Middle East Conflict and $110 Oil Trigger Risk-Off; Hong Kong Declines Led by Lenovo and Alibaba
summary: Asian equity markets sold off overnight as the escalating Middle East conflict and oil prices above $110 per barrel triggered a risk-off retreat. In Hong Kong, Lenovo (992 HK) fell 10.9%, Horizon Robotics declined 8.5%, and Alibaba fell 6.3%. The ASX in Australia also closed lower, with Nick Scali Ltd falling ~15.5% on profit concerns.
key_facts: US equity futures also lower: S&P -1%, Nasdaq -1.6%

headline: IEA Warns Diesel Market Constraints From Middle East Conflict Could Persist Into 2027
summary: The International Energy Agency cautioned in its latest monthly report that diesel market constraints stemming from the US-Iran conflict and Gulf shipping disruptions could persist well into 2027. Global petroleum production is projected to fall from a record 106.3 million barrels per day in 2025 to 101.1 million bpd in 2026.
key_facts: IEA warns diesel constraints may persist into 2027
Global petroleum production forecast: 101.1M bpd in 2026 (down from record 106.3M bpd in 2025)
At least 18 vessel attacks across Gulf region in two weeks
War severely disrupted flows through Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb

headline: G7 Agrees to Release 100 Million Barrels From Emergency Reserves to Ease Oil Market Tightness
summary: The Group of Seven major economies agreed to release a combined 100 million barrels of crude oil and diesel from emergency strategic reserves to counter supply disruptions caused by Middle East conflict. The release aims to cushion the impact of attacks on Gulf shipping and Saudi energy infrastructure.
key_facts: G7 to release 100M barrels of crude oil and diesel from emergency reserves
Action follows Gulf shipping attacks and Saudi Aramco strike
Brent crude still above $110/bbl despite release announcement

headline: DexCom (DXCM) Among S&P 500's Worst Performers on Oct 22, Shares Down ~6.4%
summary: DexCom shares fell approximately 6.4% on October 22, ranking among the S&P 500's largest decliners alongside AT&T and Netflix on a risk-off trading day driven by Middle East tensions and oil prices.
key_facts: Among S&P 500's worst performers on the day

headline: Charles River Laboratories (CRL) Gains +9.3% to Lead S&P 500 Alongside SMCI on Oct 22
summary: Charles River Laboratories shares rose approximately 9.3% on October 22, among the top S&P 500 gainers on the day alongside Super Micro Computer. The move was part of a broad divergence within the index as Middle East-related risk-off sentiment weighed on tech and communication services names.

headline: Meta Raises Full-Year 2026 AI Capex Guidance to ~$135–145B; EPS Guidance Upgraded to $7.65–$7.75
summary: Meta raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.65–$7.75 per share (vs. prior $7.10–$7.25) alongside Q3 results. Capital expenditure guidance was significantly raised to support AI infrastructure buildout, with some reports citing a range near $135–145 billion, though the company has not officially confirmed that figure. AI investments and the Muse AI platform were highlighted as growth drivers.
key_facts: Full-year 2026 adj EPS guidance raised to $7.65–$7.75 (from $7.10–$7.25)
Capex guidance significantly raised for AI infrastructure
Muse AI platform highlighted as growth driver

headline: IBM Software Revenue Rises 8% in Q3 2026 as AI-Driven Demand Accelerates
summary: IBM's Software segment posted 8% revenue growth in Q3 2026, outpacing the company's overall 5% revenue increase, reflecting strong demand for AI-powered enterprise software solutions. Infrastructure segment rose 4%, while Consulting was flat. Year-to-date free cash flow reached $7.8 billion.
key_facts: FY free cash flow forecast: >$1B above prior year

headline: Tesla FSD Attach Rate Exceeds 75% of New North America Deliveries in Q3; Subscriptions Up 67% YoY
summary: Tesla reported that its Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature attached to more than 75% of new vehicle deliveries in North America during Q3 2026, a significant milestone for the company's software revenue ambitions. FSD subscriptions grew 67% year-over-year globally.
key_facts: FSD attach rate >75% of new NA deliveries in Q3 2026

headline: AT&T Posts Best Consolidated Service Revenue Growth in 4+ Years in Q3 2026; Adds 1M+ Advanced Connectivity Customers
summary: AT&T achieved its best consolidated service revenue growth in over four years during Q3 2026, adding more than one million Advanced Connectivity customers (fiber, fixed wireless, postpaid phone) for the second straight quarter. The company grew converged relationships by approximately 350,000 and is on track for 60 million fiber locations by end of 2030.
key_facts: Best consolidated service revenue growth in 4+ years
On track for 60M fiber locations by end-2030

headline: Netflix Q4 2026 Revenue Guidance $13.4B; Full-Year 2026 Guided to $51.1B
summary: Following Q3 results, Netflix guided Q4 2026 revenue to $13.4 billion with a 26.0% operating margin, including an approximately 120 basis-point headwind from recent headcount reductions. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is $51.1 billion.

headline: American Airlines Fuel Expense Surges 67.5% YoY in Q3 2026, Adding $1.9B in Costs Due to Middle East Oil Spike
summary: American Airlines disclosed that fuel expense surged 67.5% year-over-year in Q3 2026, adding $1.9 billion in costs compared to the prior year, driven entirely by the Middle East oil price shock. Despite the surge, the airline achieved the best unit cost performance among US network carriers with CASM-ex rising only 3.0%.
key_facts: Primary driver: Middle East oil price spike
CASM-ex +3.0% YoY (best among US network carriers)

headline: October 22 Morning Preview: Middle East Tensions, Oil at $111, Tesla and Meta Earnings Drive Premarket
summary: The October 22 morning preview highlights Middle East tensions and oil prices near $111 per barrel as the primary market-moving theme, alongside Q3 earnings reports from Tesla, IBM, and other major companies. S&P 500 futures are broadly lower as inflation concerns resurface from the energy spike.
key_facts: Brent crude near $111/bbl as of Oct 22 morning preview
Tesla and Meta Q3 earnings driving premarket sentiment

headline: NordFX Market Pulse Oct 22: Risk-Off Tone as Oil Tops $110, Gold Near $4,100 and Fed Meeting Looms
summary: NordFX's daily market pulse for October 22 captures a risk-off sentiment with oil above $110, gold near $4,100, and markets cautious ahead of the Fed's October 28 rate decision. Equities in Asia and European futures are lower, with the US premarket also under pressure.

headline: Newsquawk Oct 22 US Opening: Earnings Season in Full Swing; Oil Above $110, Yields Elevated
summary: Newsquawk's October 22 US opening bulletin covers a busy earnings day (IBM, Tesla, Meta, Valero, American Airlines, Honeywell, Dow, AT&T, Blackstone) against a backdrop of oil prices above $110 per barrel and 10-year Treasury yields at 5.12–5.13%, creating headwinds for equities.
key_facts: Busy Q3 earnings day: IBM, Tesla, Meta, Valero, AAL, HON, DOW, T, BX
Earnings results broadly mixed to bullish vs. expectations
